q: How does a tanker cleaning station count steam and effluent emissions?
title: Tanker cleaning stations: steam and effluent
short: Boiler fuel used to make cleaning steam is Scope 1 for the station. Wastewater sent to a treatment plant is Scope 3 category 5. The trucking company that pays for cleaning counts it as a purchased service in its own Scope 3.
audience: Chemical tanker cleaning stations and the transporters who use them

p: Boiler fuel per month and the number of tankers cleaned.
Divide the station's emissions by tankers cleaned if a customer asks for a per-wash figure, and say how it was split.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.
